---
title: "Milestone 1a: empty-lattice validation"
description: "fcc free-electron bands against the analytic folded parabolas."
date: 2026-11-05
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
from fractions import Fraction

import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from jaxdft import (
    empty,
    fcc_lattice,
    PlaneWaveBasis,
    band_structure,
    free_electron_bands,
    kpath,
    special_points_fcc,
)
from jaxdft.hamiltonian.operator import SENTINEL_FACTOR
from jaxdft.plotting import style

style.enable()

a = 10.26  # Bohr, the Si lattice constant (the empty lattice is scale-free)
lattice = fcc_lattice(a, unit="Bohr")
E0 = 0.5 * (2 * np.pi / a) ** 2  # energy unit 1/2 (2 pi / a)^2, Ha
ecut = 12.5 * E0
eps_mach = np.finfo(np.float64).eps
tolerance = 1e-10  # Ha, acceptance-test tolerance (tests/support/tolerances.py)

points = special_points_fcc()
path = kpath(lattice, points, [["L", "G", "X", "U"], ["K", "G"]], n_points=200)
basis = PlaneWaveBasis.build(lattice, path.kpoints, ecut)
n_bands = int(basis.n_pw.min())
bands = band_structure(empty(lattice), basis, n_bands)
reference = free_electron_bands(lattice, path.kpoints, n_bands)

computed = np.asarray(bands.eigenvalues)
analytic = np.asarray(reference)
deviation = np.abs(computed - analytic)
max_dev = float(deviation.max())
# The interpretation relies on these; a regression must break the render.
assert max_dev <= tolerance
assert np.all(computed <= ecut)  # every plotted eigenvalue is in the exact, complete range
```

This document validates Milestone 1a against the first rung of the validation
ladder: the exact band structure of a free electron in an fcc cell. The
physics, conventions and acceptance criteria are in the
[theory post](../theory/01a_empty_lattice.qmd).

## Setup

- fcc lattice, $a$ = `{python} f"{a}"` Bohr ($\Omega$ = `{python} f"{float(lattice.volume):.2f}"` Bohr³).
- Energy unit $E_0 = \tfrac12(2\pi/a)^2$ = `{python} f"{E0:.5f}"` Ha.
- Cutoff $E_\text{cut}$ = `{python} f"{ecut / E0:.1f}"` $E_0$ = `{python} f"{ecut:.4f}"` Ha.
- Path L–Γ–X–U|K–Γ with `{python} f"{len(path.kpoints)}"` k-points, computed in
  one vmapped call. $N_\text{PW}$ ranges from `{python} f"{int(basis.n_pw.min())}"`
  to `{python} f"{int(basis.n_pw.max())}"` across the path, padded to
  $N_\text{pad}$ = `{python} f"{basis.n_pad}"`, and `{python} f"{n_bands}"` bands
  are computed at every k.

All eigenvalues below the cutoff are exact in this basis, so the computed bands
should equal the analytic folded parabolas to rounding.

## Band structure

Lines are the computed bands. Points are the analytic reference
$\varepsilon_{n\mathbf{k}}$ = $n$-th smallest $\tfrac12|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}|^2$,
shown at every fifth k-point. Hover a point for values; drag or scroll to pan
and zoom.

```{python}
#| column: page-inset
#| echo: false
E_MAX = 8.0  # E0, top of the plotted window
x = np.asarray(path.distance)
keep = np.flatnonzero(computed.min(axis=0) / E0 <= E_MAX)

lines = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"distance": x[i], "band": int(n), "energy": computed[i, n] / E0, "source": "computed (jaxdft)"}
        for n in keep
        for i in range(len(x))
    ]
)
marks = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "distance": x[i],
            "band": int(n) + 1,
            "energy": analytic[i, n] / E0,
            "energy_Ha": analytic[i, n],
            "deviation_Ha": deviation[i, n],
            "source": "analytic folded bands",
        }
        for n in keep
        for i in range(0, len(x), 5)
        if analytic[i, n] / E0 <= E_MAX
    ]
)

ticks = np.asarray(path.tick_positions)
label_lookup = "{" + ", ".join(f"'{t:.6f}': '{lab}'" for t, lab in zip(ticks, path.tick_labels)) + "}"
x_axis = alt.X(
    "distance:Q",
    title=None,
    scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, float(x[-1])], nice=False),
    axis=alt.Axis(values=[float(t) for t in ticks], labelExpr=f"{label_lookup}[format(datum.value, '.6f')]", grid=True),
)
y_axis = alt.Y("energy:Q", title="Energy (E₀)", scale=alt.Scale(domain=[0, E_MAX]))
colour = alt.Color(
    "source:N",
    title=None,
    scale=alt.Scale(domain=["computed (jaxdft)", "analytic folded bands"], range=[style.SERIES[0], style.SERIES[1]]),
)

line_layer = alt.Chart(lines).mark_line(clip=True).encode(x=x_axis, y=y_axis, color=colour, detail="band:N")
point_layer = (
    alt.Chart(marks)
    .mark_point(clip=True, size=40, stroke=style.SURFACE, strokeWidth=1)
    .encode(
        x=x_axis,
        y=y_axis,
        color=colour,
        tooltip=[
            alt.Tooltip("band:Q", title="band"),
            alt.Tooltip("energy:Q", title="energy (E₀)", format=".4f"),
            alt.Tooltip("energy_Ha:Q", title="energy (Ha)", format=".6f"),
            alt.Tooltip("deviation_Ha:Q", title="|computed − analytic| (Ha)", format=".1e"),
        ],
    )
)
(line_layer + point_layer).properties(width=style.WIDTH, height=style.HEIGHT).interactive()
```

## Deviation from the analytic bands

```{python}
#| echo: false
n_exact = int(np.sum(deviation == 0))
n_total = deviation.size
agreement = (
    "bit-for-bit identical"
    if max_dev == 0
    else f"equal to within {max_dev:.1e} Ha ({max_dev / (eps_mach * ecut):.1f} ε_mach E_cut)"
)
```

Over all `{python} f"{n_total}"` eigenvalues on the path, the computed and
analytic values are `{python} agreement`;
`{python} f"{n_exact}"` of them agree exactly. Exact agreement is what we should
expect here, and it is not a deep check by itself. The empty-lattice matrix is
diagonal, so `eigh` returns its diagonal entries, sorted, without rounding. The
library's analytic reference evaluates the same $\tfrac12|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}|^2$
with the same arithmetic. The acceptance tolerance of
`{python} f"{tolerance:.0e}"` Ha is reserved for comparisons with non-identical
arithmetic.

The independent checks are in the acceptance tests. There, the reference is a
separate NumPy enumeration over twice the proven Miller bound, computed by a
different arithmetic route ($\mathbf{k}B + \mathbf{m}B$ rather than
$(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{m})B$), and itself checked against the hand-derived
degeneracy table. A non-diagonal Hamiltonian is checked against eigenvalues
computed independently in NumPy.

## Degeneracies at the high-symmetry points

Each point is computed with its own basis and all $N_\text{PW}(\mathbf{k})$ bands.
The table shows the lowest six levels of the computed spectrum, grouped at
$10^{-6}$ Ha. The comparison is with the library's analytic reference grouped
the same way. (The acceptance tests compare instead with an independent NumPy
enumeration and with the hand-derived table in the theory post.)

```{python}
#| echo: false
def levels(e, atol=1e-6, n=6):
    e = np.sort(np.asarray(e))
    groups = [[e[0]]]
    for v in e[1:]:
        if v - groups[-1][-1] <= atol:
            groups[-1].append(v)
        else:
            groups.append([v])
    return [(float(np.mean(g)), len(g)) for g in groups][:n]


def fmt(levs):
    return ", ".join(f"{Fraction(v / E0).limit_denominator(8)} ({d})" for v, d in levs)


rows = []
for label in ["G", "X", "L", "W", "K", "U"]:
    k = np.asarray(points[label])[None]
    b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(lattice, k, ecut)
    e = np.asarray(band_structure(empty(lattice), b, int(b.n_pw[0])).eigenvalues[0])
    e = e[e <= ecut]
    ref = np.asarray(free_electron_bands(lattice, k, len(e))[0])
    got, want = levels(e), levels(ref)
    worst = max(abs(g[0] - w[0]) for g, w in zip(got, want))
    rows.append(
        {
            "point": "Γ" if label == "G" else label,
            "N_PW": int(b.n_pw[0]),
            "lowest levels in E₀ (degeneracy)": fmt(got),
            "degeneracies match": [d for _, d in got] == [d for _, d in want],
            "max level error (Ha)": f"{worst:.1e}",
        }
    )
# The interpretation below relies on this; a regression must break the render.
assert all(r["degeneracies match"] for r in rows)
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

## Basis size and the cost of padding

The theory post chose one padded Miller-index list per k-point over a single
shared candidate set containing every $\mathcal{B}_\mathbf{k}$ (radius
$G_\text{max} + |\mathrm{W}|$). The table compares the two over the six
high-symmetry points for a range of cutoffs. $N_\text{asym} = \Omega(2E_\text{cut})^{3/2}/6\pi^2$
is the asymptotic basis size. Dense diagonalisation costs the cube of the
padded size.

```{python}
#| echo: false
ks = np.array([np.asarray(points[p]) for p in ["G", "X", "L", "W", "K", "U"]])
r_bz = float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(points["W"]) @ np.asarray(lattice.reciprocal)))
rows = []
for E in [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0]:
    b = PlaneWaveBasis.build(lattice, ks, E)
    shared_radius = np.sqrt(2 * E) + r_bz
    shared = int(PlaneWaveBasis.build(lattice, np.zeros((1, 3)), 0.5 * shared_radius**2).n_pw[0])
    n_asym = float(lattice.volume) * (2 * E) ** 1.5 / (6 * np.pi**2)
    rows.append(
        {
            "E_cut (Ha)": f"{E:g}",
            "N_PW range": f"{int(b.n_pw.min())}–{int(b.n_pw.max())}",
            "N_asym": f"{n_asym:.1f}",
            "per-k padded N_pad": b.n_pad,
            "shared set": shared,
            "size ratio": f"{shared / b.n_pad:.2f}",
            "eigh cost ratio": f"{(shared / b.n_pad) ** 3:.1f}×",
        }
    )
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

## Interpretation

The computed bands reproduce the folded free-electron parabolas everywhere on
the path, including the band counts: no plane wave below the cutoff is missing
at any k-point. The padding sentinel (`{python} f"{SENTINEL_FACTOR:g}"`
$E_\text{cut}$) leaves the physical eigenvalues untouched, as it should if
the padding is exactly decoupled. That holds here for the
`{python} f"{int(np.sum(np.asarray(basis.n_pw) < basis.n_pad))}"` of
`{python} f"{len(path.kpoints)}"` path k-points that carry padding.

Every degeneracy at the high-symmetry points matches the analytic count. In
particular, the U and K spectra are identical, which is why the band plot is
continuous across the U|K jump; only the slope changes there. The bands meet
the zone boundary in pairs (at X the lowest level is doubly degenerate) and the
parabolas cross freely, as they must without a potential to open gaps.
Milestone 1b introduces the gaps.

What this does **not** validate is anything involving coupling between plane
waves. The empty-lattice Hamiltonian is diagonal, so the structure-factor
sign, the $1/\Omega$ normalisation of $\tilde V(\mathbf{G}-\mathbf{G}')$, and
the decoupling of padding under a non-diagonal term are not tested here. The
last of these is covered by the property tests, using a test-only coupling
term. The first two are Milestone 1b's job.
